t: Surena's horse archers stayed out of reach of the Roman javelins, and the Romans' close formations could not drive them off or fight back, while his cataphracts charged whenever the Romans loosened their ranks.

Crassus refused Artavasdes II's offer of a route through Armenia and of reinforcements, and marched straight through Mesopotamia; Surena, whose force was heavily outnumbered, had been sent only to scout and harass him.
Plutarch gives about 20,000 Roman dead and 10,000 prisoners. Gaius Cassius Longinus led about 10,000 survivors back to Syria and defended the province against Parthian attacks.
dyk: The Parthians kept up their supply of arrows by using thousands of camels, which Crassus had hoped would run out before his legionaries gave way.
ev: Crassus, Pompey and Caesar renew their alliance at Ravenna and Luca, and Crassus arranges to have Syria as his province
Crassus invades the Parthian client-state of Osroene while Surena defeats and executes Mithridates IV at Seleucia
In the spring Crassus rejects Armenia's offer and marches through Mesopotamia
Surena's horse archers and cataphracts defeat the Romans near Carrhae, and Publius Crassus dies with his force
Crassus is killed at a truce meeting, and Cassius leads about 10,000 survivors back to Syria
A Parthian invasion is stopped and repulsed by Publius Ventidius Bassus
Mark Antony invades Parthia in the Atropatene campaign, which also fails

f.date: 9 June 53 BCE, the date given by Ovid in Book 6 of the Fasti
f.place: Near the ancient town of Carrhae, present-day Harran, Turkey, on the plain of northern Mesopotamia
f.sides: The Roman Republic under Marcus Licinius Crassus, with seven legions of about 28,000 to 35,000 heavy infantry, about 4,000 light infantry and 4,000 cavalry according to Plutarch; the Parthian Empire under the spahbod Surena, with roughly 10,000 men
f.outcome: Crassus was killed when truce negotiations turned violent. Most of his army was killed or captured; Plutarch gives about 20,000 killed and 10,000 captured, and Parthian casualties as minimal.
